post.0:
I lost 87 to 63, and the game turned on Ben's very last placement: Party Crasher let him join Cal on Makeover, and he rearranged a 19-resource pile into 7 red, 8 yellow, 4 blue, beating me on yellow by one and Cal on red by one for a +30 sweep. I had counted every open yellow space for his reach (5 at most) and simply forgot that a taken Makeover was reachable through Party Crasher, which I'd even buried once in round one. Before that my game was decent: Big Dilute plus Harvest stole red and held yellow for +12 in round two, and cashing 15 blue through Recruit Twice in round three was efficient. But I passed too many recruits in rounds one and two holding for contests, and five members was far too thin next to Ben's Patriarch (+14) and Cal's Mob (+14). Ben's churn engine (Trendsetters, Bargain Bin, Patroness) quietly fed him blue and followers on every shop move, mine included.

FEEL: Gather | 3 | 3 | yes | solid red plus a follower kicker, Cal used it well to fund Mob.
FEEL: Walk-In | 3 | 4 | yes | a free member plus Guest Book trigger in round one felt great; the gift of red to rivals is a real but small cost.
FEEL: Promote | 4 | 3 | yes | with Recruiter and Deprogrammers stacked it was the strongest red space; one swap was +5 red and a follower swing.
FEEL: Demote | 3 | 3 | yes | same engine as Promote, and the Old Maid hot-potato swap made it nasty.
FEEL: Recruit a Member | 2 | 2 | yes | a free member in round three is fine but rarely the best use of a late minion.
FEEL: Harvest | 4 | 4 | yes | any-color income let me steal round two red outright; flexible and always a real option.
FEEL: Trade Seeds | 3 | 2 | yes | useful for a last-moment contest tweak, but the reordering option list made me undo my own swap.
FEEL: Dilute | 4 | 4 | yes | recoloring Cal's 2 red away to win red was my favorite move; real interaction.
FEEL: Big Dilute | 4 | 4 | yes | six changes reshape the whole table; strong denial but every recolored cube still lands with the rival somewhere.
FEEL: Melting Pot | 3 | 3 | yes | reliable +5 with three member colors, mostly a raw-gain space.
FEEL: Makeover | 5 | 3 | yes | decides round three; whoever holds the biggest pile picks their +10s, and with Party Crasher it decided all three.
FEEL: Savings | 2 | 2 | yes | plain blue, the bury rider mostly helps whoever holds Bargain Bin.
FEEL: Out of Style | 3 | 2 | yes | +5 or +6 when the shop is blue-heavy, but it feeds Bargain Bin and Patroness for the blue player.
FEEL: Peek | 3 | 3 | yes | biggest flat blue; stacking the pile mattered little in round three.
FEEL: Recruit Twice | 4 | 4 | yes | cashing 15 in one turn and denying Ben the same was a good moment; the extra recruit is the real value in round three.
FEEL: Bury | 3 | 3 | yes | burying HR for +6 blue was both income and denial; its value scales oddly with whatever expensive card is out.
FEEL: Spree | 2 | 2 | yes | three recruits is only good if you have the pile to spend, never came up for me.
FEEL: Guest Book | 2 | 3 | yes | three triggers for 6 yellow early, then dead from round one on with only three colors.
FEEL: Recruiter | 3 | 2 | unsure | looked thin at draft but Promote and Demote fed Cal +2 red repeatedly; the artifact I'd least want to pick, though, since it depends on rivals swapping.
FEEL: Customs | 4 | 4 | yes | a free Walk-In draw that made my yellow nearly immune to Dilute; quietly excellent.
FEEL: Volunteer | 2 | 3 | yes | 1 for 1 plus a Guest Book trigger, fine filler.
FEEL: Window Dressers | 3 | 3 | yes | 3 bodies for 4 is fair; the churn helped Ben's Bargain Bin more than me.
FEEL: Drifters | 2 | 2 | yes | 3 for 2 bodies, I passed every time on rate.
FEEL: HR | 3 | 2 | unsure | 10 for 4 is bad unless you build triples; I buried it mainly because Ben's wide cult could use it.
FEEL: Extra Hand | 2 | 1 | unsure | 9 for one follower and a once-per-game minion never pencils out this late.
FEEL: Patriarch | 4 | 3 | yes | at 6 cost it scored Ben +14; I priced it for my 5-member cult and missed that it's a monster in a wide one.
FEEL: Party Crasher | 5 | 4 | unsure | the card that won the game; joining a taken Makeover is a huge ceiling for 4 cost, and I buried it once without respecting it.
FEEL: Dyer | 2 | 2 | yes | 7 for 1 plus 2 yellow at round three, never close.
META: Contests and the resource pile give the game a real tension, and the interaction spaces (Dilute, Promote/Demote, Makeover) produced the best moments. What isn't working is how much a wide member count snowballs: Patriarch and Mob each scored 14 at game end while my efficient buy-followers line left me with 5 members and no end-game bonus. The one thing I'd change first is Party Crasher onto Makeover: letting a second player into the round-three rearrange turns the last placement into a three-contest sweep with no counterplay; either block Party Crasher on center spaces or cap Makeover to one color.
post.1:
I won 87 to 63 to 58, and honestly it was decided on the very last placement: Ava cashed almost her whole pile into followers on Recruit Twice and Melting Pot, which left 7 yellow, 6 red for Cal and nobody but me in blue, so Party Crasher onto Cal's Makeover let me remix 19 resources into 8 yellow, 7 red, 4 blue and take all three +10s at once. Before that I was behind Ava; the swap war with Cal (Demote taking Deprogrammers, Panel taking back Trendsetters, Anarchist dumping Old Maid on him, then him Demoting it right back onto me through Loyalists) was the fun middle of the game. Patriarch quietly paid +14 at the end because I ended up with 28 bodies, which is a lot for a 6-cost card. My mistake was buying Loyalists while Cal still had Demote open; I'd pointed out that Loyalists doesn't guard itself and then walked straight into it. The last-placement seat plus Makeover plus Party Crasher was simply too much power for one turn in round III.

META: The swap layer (Promote, Demote, Panel, Anarchist, Old Maid, Loyalists, Deprogrammers, Recruiter) is where the interesting decisions live, and it reads clearly at the table. What isn't working is round III's last placement: Makeover plus last seat (or Party Crasher) lets one player pick every contest, so holding resources all game is pointless if someone can remix at the end, and buying followers 1 to 1 is the safer line for everyone else. First change: make Makeover only rearrange a capped number (say up to 6), or have Party Crasher's join not work on the center ring.
post.2:
I finished last with 58 to Ben's 87. The game turned in round III's first turns: I sat on Scouts instead of firing it with Patroness, and Ben used Anarchist to dump Old Maid on me (-6) and then Promote took Patroness itself, so my best engine became his. I got some back by Demoting Old Maid onto his unprotected Loyalists, but the last placement killed me. I forgot Party Crasher could join a taken space, and Ben's Party Crasher into my Makeover turned his pile into 7 red, one more than my 6. My last 1-follower buy cost me a tie on +10, and he swept all three round III contests. Lesson: in round III the player who places last, with a big pile and any way onto Makeover, decides every contest, so my holdings had to clear his ceiling and not just the open spaces.
